newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of July 7, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - The Boston Globe has developed an intranet system that is the envy of newpapers around the country. The effort, led by the IS team, allows employees to access, among other things, an employee directory, human resources, the cafeteria and wire service newsfeeds, according to the July 7 edition of PCWeek.

Sybase Inc is set to release its OLAP server for its Sybase IQ database, allowing it to catch up with its rivals, Oracle and Informix, which already offer OLAP servers for their databases, PCWeek said.

COMPUTERWORLD - For those caught between mainframe and client/server technology, hybrid systems are the latest solution, ComputerWorld said in its July 7 edition. Major application vendors like SAP AG are moving to IBM's S/390 and AS/400, making the R/3 port the crown jewel in IBM's efforts to lure back to the mainframe.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - In a move aimed at increasing efficiency and stemming financial losses, Apple Computer Inc is set to unveil a plan to shift some system assembly to the channel, Computer Reseller News reported in its July 7 issue.
The changes in manufacturing and distribution strategy should start this fall, when Apple's fiscal year begins, and is expected to be unveiled in Boston next month.

INFOWORLD - Vendors such as IBM and Packard Bell NEC plan later this year to offer the newest thing in mobile computing: the mega-notebooks, or full-function systems equivalent to a desktop computer, InfoWorld said in its July 7 edition. The notebooks will weigh about eight pounds, and range in price from $5,000 to $6,000.

INFORMATION WEEK - Many large enterprise customers are returning to International Business Machines Corp mainframe computers, which they say offer better performance for the price than rival client-server systems, Information Week reported July 7.
Hewlett-Packard Co plans to introduce a high-end line of workstations that will compete with Silicon Graphics Inc machines in the market for sophisticated 3-D modeling, Information Week reported.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - Micron Technology Inc is making about 30 million 16-Mbit units of DRAM a month, making it the world's largets DRAM producer, surpassing Samsung electronics Co Ltd, Electronic Buyers' News reported on July 7.

Cyrix Corp, will not rush to match Intel Corp's Merced chip, which is due in 1998, choosing instead to wait until the market matures, Electronic Buyers' News reported on July 7. EBN also said Cyrix and Advanced Micro Devices are plannng their own second-generation versions of the MMX instruction set.

MACWEEK - Apple Computer and its licensees are close to a deal for Mac OS 8, sources told MacWeek in its July 7 issue. The negotiating parties tentatively agreed to terms to ease the arrival of common hardware reference platform systems.
